title: Wall Sections: What to Include, Examples, and How to Draw One in Revit
summary: What a wall section shows, the layers and connections it needs, examples by wall type, and how to draw one in Revit, from the foundation to the roof.
body_markdown:
## Wall section examples by wall type


The layers change with the structure and the cladding. Here are six common[wall types](https://www.pirros.com/revit/how-to/create-and-change-wall-types) .


### Wood stud wall section


Light-frame wood studs hold cavity insulation, with sheathing and a water-resistive barrier outside and gypsum board inside. Platform framing puts a rim board at each floor, and the sill plate sits on the foundation with anchor bolts. The energy code (the IECC, or ASHRAE 90.1 for commercial work) sets how much insulation the wall needs. NFPA 285 can apply where exterior walls are fire-retardant-treated wood on a Type III building; typical Type V wood construction is exempt.


### Metal stud wall section with brick veneer


Cold-formed steel studs carry gypsum board inside and exterior sheathing outside, with the air and water barrier and continuous insulation on the sheathing. The brick sits in front of an air space, tied back to the studs. Through-wall flashing and weeps go at its base, over openings and at shelf angles in taller buildings. TMS 402 governs the veneer itself: tie spacing, the air space and support at each shelf angle. The energy code (the IECC or ASHRAE 90.1) sets the continuous insulation, and on Type I to IV buildings an assembly with foam plastic insulation or a combustible water-resistive barrier needs NFPA 285 approval.


### CMU wall section


Concrete masonry units carry the load, grouted and reinforced where the structure needs it, with bond beams where floors and roof bear. The block is insulated outside under a veneer or panel, or furred and insulated inside. It is flashed and weeped like any masonry wall.


### Concrete wall section


Cast-in-place or precast concrete forms the structure. Insulation goes outside the concrete or on furring inside it. Below grade, the section shows the waterproofing, drainage board and footing.


### Curtain wall section


A curtain wall carries no floor loads; it hangs from the slab edges. The section shows the anchors at each floor, the insulated spandrel in front of the slab, and the firestopping between slab edge and curtain wall. That firestopping is a perimeter fire barrier, tested as a system to ASTM E2307.


### Mass timber wall section


A cross-laminated timber (CLT) or other mass timber panel forms the wall, with continuous insulation, an air and water barrier, and cladding on a rainscreen outside. The section shows how the floor panels bear on or hang from the wall, and how the barriers stay continuous past them.
